p.i: AT, o Gigantis Impium tandem caput, Polo sedere difce iudicem Deum. Ille haud retorto, cuncta cernit lumine. Paratus vltor improbi conaminis. Ergo Iuuentus horrida & ferox, suis Fidens lacertis, & polo ferens minas, Sensitque fulmen, & pollo missas faces, Senfit paratas in necem suam manus. Non militares, at tenellas virginis Olim sonantem Palladis sic Aegida Sensere Thorcus, & minax trunco Nimas, Et quos recepit in sinum parens suum Tellus, caduco concrematos fulmine. Ergo superba monstra concitum mare Hausit rapaci vortice: & cete fera Expofla ficco, & deftituta littore, Feras reliquit impias cibum feris. Horrenda sed qua fata iam iamque imminent Crudo tyranno, ni refipifcit, accipe. Si non senile fregerit guttur patris Sinu parentis educata filia, Vltrix futura fratris, heu! latho dati, Vltrix futura matris, heu! latho data, A patre habenas & petens rerum sibi Adulterifque, queis latus fit fortius,

page.notes: Printed text is in italic throughout. The printed verse uses long s-like forms, which are rendered as plain s. Some letters are visually uncertain in the scan (e.g. "Thorcus", "Nimas", "Expofla", "cete", "latho", "Tiestetur" at the foot, which is the catchword as printed and may be read as "Tieftetur"); the line "Adulterifque, queis" is partly faint. Words such as "Crudo tyranno, ni refipifcit" and "Horrenda sed qua fata" are readable but could contain small errors. Possible printing errors: "Expofla" and "Feras reliquit impias cibum feris" as printed; "Tellus, caduco concrematos fulmine" as printed. Verify "Thorcus" (possibly Thoracus/Thorax), "Nimas" and "Adulterifque" against the original.
